briefing.text: The bh43 tables (a clinical sample table and a mutation MAF for an upper tract urothelial carcinoma cohort) appear to hold no DNA-methylation data and no EpiC subtype or cluster column. Check the clinical headers yourself for subtype, cluster or methylation fields. If they are absent, the hypothesis is still about this study's own cohort and genes (UTUC, FGFR3), so under the benchmark convention the label is True or False, decided from the closest proxies plus established biology, not Not verifiable.
briefing.reason: The missing methylation/subtype variables invite a wrong 'Not verifiable'; the label convention says own-cohort claims are True/False.

briefing.text: When deriving FGFR3 mutation status, count unique Tumor_Sample_Barcode values and use every sample in data_clinical_sample.txt as the denominator, treating samples with no MAF rows as wild-type. Count the samples from the file rather than trusting any stated number (the library recorded 31).
briefing.reason: Using only MAF samples as the denominator biases the FGFR3 frequency and any comparison by FGFR3 status.

briefing.text: In urothelial carcinoma, FGFR3-mutant tumours are usually luminal-papillary, low-grade and have low mutational burden, and in UTUC FGFR3 mutation has been linked to a distinct methylation-defined epigenetic cluster. You can count FGFR3 hotspot mutations (R248C, S249C, G370C, Y373C, K650E) per sample and compare TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS between mutants and non-mutants, but this is only a supporting proxy: it cannot identify EpiC clusters or methylation state. The library wrote this from domain knowledge; no source was retrieved, so treat which cluster carries FGFR3 as unverified.
briefing.reason: It names the closest testable proxy and its limits, and warns that the library's cluster attribution is unverified.

briefing.text: The library flags the hypothesis's pairing of the name 'EpiC-low' with 'hypermethylation' as something to examine: the subtype name may or may not match the methylation state it is said to have. Reason explicitly about which EpiC cluster the hypothesis describes and whether its name, methylation direction and FGFR3 status fit together. Do not assume either way.
briefing.reason: The label probably depends on cluster identity and naming, which the data cannot show, so the teams need to reason about it on purpose.

shared_assumptions: Both teams assume, from recall, that the study named its hypermethylated cluster 'EpiC-high', so 'EpiC-low with hypermethylation' must be a swapped name; neither team has any verified source for this naming, and the 'high/low' suffix may refer to something other than methylation level (e.g. epigenetic-cluster ordering, or low expression/low mutation burden).

Both assume the hypothesis is a reversal of a study finding rather than the finding itself; under the benchmark convention the unreversed finding is equally likely a priori, so the label hinges entirely on that unverified recall.
Both treat each of the 30 Tumor_Sample_Barcodes as an independent tumour and FGFR3 missense calls as equivalent to activating hotspot mutations.
unused_evidence: The MAF Hotspot and Annotation_Status columns were not reported as used to confirm that all 15 FGFR3 calls are canonical activating hotspots.
t_ref_count/t_alt_count (and n_* counts) columns exist; team-b stated VAF is unavailable without checking whether these columns are populated.
TMB_NONSYNONYMOUS per sample: neither team asked whether the low-TMB FGFR3-mutant group corresponds to a 'low' subtype under an alternative reading of the suffix.
Mutations in DNA-methylation machinery genes (e.g. DNMT3A, TET2, IDH1/2) were not cross-tabulated against FGFR3 as a methylation proxy; team-a's cross-tab covered histone modifiers only.
unresolved_weak_points: Team-a: label depends on recalled naming (EpiC-high = hypermethylated); reported, not resolved.
Team-b: label 'rests wholly' on the same naming assumption, and an earlier team-b run leaned True for the same reasoning; reported, not resolved. Team-b confidence 0.55 is close to a coin flip.
second_readings: 'EpiC-low' could denote low expression of some epigenetic/immune signature, or a cluster with low mutation burden, rather than low methylation; under that reading 'EpiC-low' being hypermethylated and FGFR3-enriched is not self-contradictory.
The hypothesis could be read as the study's own finding stated verbatim (label True) rather than a swapped finding; the data alone cannot discriminate.
challenge.verdict: Low-to-moderate trust: both teams agree only because they share one unverified recall of the subtype naming, which neither tested and one team's own earlier run read the opposite way; the data hold no subtype or methylation variable to break the tie.

questions.question: QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Your False label rests on recalled naming (EpiC-high = hypermethylated). What independent evidence, in the data or in a verifiable definition, supports that the 'high/low' suffix refers to methylation level rather than to some other axis such as mutation burden? If you cannot cite any, does your confidence of 0.72 still hold, and does the label change?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Cross-tabulate FGFR3 hotspot status against TMB tertiles and against the hypermutated samples (19T, 30T, 2T, 28T). If FGFR3-mutant tumours cluster in the low-TMB group, does that make an alternative reading of 'EpiC-low' (a low-burden epigenetic cluster) plausible, and does that change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Check mutations in DNA-methylation machinery genes (DNMT3A, TET1/2, IDH1/2) by FGFR3 status. Does any pattern bear on which FGFR3 group would be hypermethylated, and does it change your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: An earlier team-b run leaned True and the current one says False, both from the same naming argument. What specifically resolved that disagreement? If nothing in the data did, how do you justify choosing the swapped reading over the literal one?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: You wrote that VAF is unavailable, but the MAF has t_ref_count/t_alt_count and a Hotspot column. Check whether these are populated and whether all 15 FGFR3 calls are flagged hotspots. Does that change your FGFR3 evidence or your method?

QUESTION FROM THE DIRECTOR: Tabulate FGFR3 hotspot status against TMB (low vs high, including the hypermutated samples). If FGFR3-mutant tumours are mostly low-burden, does that support a reading where a 'low' subtype is the FGFR3-enriched one, and does that change your label?

In published molecular classifications of upper tract urothelial carcinoma based on DNA methylation and expression clustering, how are epigenetic clusters labelled 'high' and 'low' defined, and which cluster is reported as hypermethylated and enriched for FGFR3 mutation?
questions.why: Both teams' label depends entirely on recalled naming of the 'high/low' epigenetic clusters; a verified definition would settle whether the hypothesis is the original finding or a reversal.

questions.question: In urothelial carcinoma, are FGFR3-mutant tumours generally associated with a CpG island hypermethylation phenotype and with low tumour mutational burden?
questions.why: This established biology is the only basis on which the teams can link FGFR3 status to methylation in data lacking methylation measurements.

findings.question: In published molecular classifications of upper tract urothelial carcinoma based on DNA methylation and expression clustering, how are epigenetic clusters labelled 'high' and 'low' defined, and which cluster is reported as hypermethylated and enriched for FGFR3 mutation?
findings.answer: Not settled by the web. The search gateway returned HTTP 403 on every call (3 calls on 2026-11-20), so I read no page. From unverified recall only: the MSKCC UTUC study (Moss et al., Eur Urol 2017) reported a hypermethylated cluster enriched for FGFR3 mutation and luminal-papillary features. I could not verify whether that cluster is labelled 'EpiC-high' or 'EpiC-low'.

findings.question: In urothelial carcinoma, are FGFR3-mutant tumours generally associated with a CpG island hypermethylation phenotype and with low tumour mutational burden?
findings.answer: Not settled by the web (gateway HTTP 403, no page read). From unverified recall only: FGFR3-mutant tumours are generally low-grade and luminal-papillary, with lower TMB than TP53-mutant tumours. The methylation direction is mixed. In bladder cancer, CpG-island hypermethylation is more typical of invasive tumours, while in UTUC FGFR3 has been linked to a hypermethylated cluster.
